svg.title: A nurse is planning a teaching session for an 80-year-old client about a new medication schedule. Which strategies should the nurse use? (Select all that apply.)
svg.desc: Older adults learn well when sensory changes are accommodated, sessions are short, pacing is unhurried, and new content is anchored to what they already do. Aging alone does not prevent learning, and a busy, noisy setting adds distraction that shortens attention and retention.

g.text: STUDY HUB / QUESTION MAP
Older Adult Learners
Read the situation
A nurse is planning a teaching session for
an 80-year-old client about a new
medication schedule. Which strategies
should the nurse use? (Select all that
apply.)
What fits here
Speak in a normal tone at a slightly lower
pitch and face the client · Schedule
several brief sessions rather than one
long one · Allow extra time for the client
to respond to questions ·…
Why it fits
Older adults learn well when sensory
changes are accommodated, sessions are
short, pacing is unhurried, and new
content is anchored to what they already
do. Aging alone does not prevent learning,
and a busy, noisy setting adds distraction
that shortens attention and retention.
